text:
Samira N.: FYI onboarding blocked: sample-app bulk upsert failed in a way that looks like an SDK vs REST parity + auth header edge-case. REST curl works, SDK attempt fails and we saw Authorization dropped after a 307 redirect.

Samira N.: REST repro (works):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1","items":[{"text":"a","dedupe_key":"r1","meta":{"src":"csv"}},{"text":"b","dedupe_key":"r2","meta":{"src":"csv"}}]}' | jq
```

Samira N.: SDK attempt (fails / 401):
```js
// @redwood/sdk js v0.9.x
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await c.embeddings.upsertBulk({ model: 'open-embedding-1', items });
// throws 401 unauthorized
```

Samira N.: Capture from proxy shows: client POST to `/v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk` returned 307 -> Location: `/v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk/` (trailing slash), SDK followed redirect but request sent without Authorization header to the redirected URL (server returned 401). Direct curl follows redirect and keeps header (curl option `-L --location` did). Also saw 429 earlier: hosted returned 429 + Retry-After: 6 but SDK retried immediately twice and replayed the request (which, since auth was dropped, failed differently on replay).

Leo F.: Interesting. Which HTTP client is the JS SDK using under the hood? Some fetch polyfills drop credentials on cross-origin redirects unless you set redirect behavior carefully. Could be we rely on node-fetch default that strips headers on 307/308.

Samira N.: Confirmed node runtime: Node 18.8, sdk uses undici/fetch wrapper. Network trace snippet:
```
-> POST /v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk 200
<- 307 Location: /v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk/
-> POST /v1/embeddings/upsert_bulk/  // missing Authorization header
<- 401 unauthorized
```

Priya S.: This is a slightly different parity class: not just param names or missing endpoints, but transport semantics (redirect handling) causing auth loss. Fixes: (A) ensure SDK's HTTP layer preserves Authorization across redirects or transparently retry to the canonical URL without redirect; (B) normalize server-side to avoid redirects when possible (maybe canonicalize ingress to not require trailing slash); (C) add an explicit `upsert.bulk()` helper that posts to the canonical path to avoid clients hitting redirect in the first place. Also: (D) retry middleware must honor Retry-After and expose a hook so SDK retries don't silently replay side-effects.

Ops Bot: rate-limiter: api_key=* returned 429 at 1803007788, Retry-After: 6s

Leo F.: Agreed. Dev plan: 1) change fetch wrapper to use `redirect: 'manual'` and handle Location responses by issuing a new request while copying safe headers (Authorization) — or better, follow the redirect but ensure headers are preserved; 2) add canonicalization test in integration: request to path with/without trailing slash must behave identically without triggering loss of auth; 3) add `upsertBulk` convenience that targets the canonical endpoint; 4) update retry logic to parse Retry-After and surface `onRetry` callback; 5) add e2e that simulates a 307 redirect followed by a 401 if auth dropped to assert SDK keeps header.

Doc Lead: I'll add a short onboarding note to sample-app quickstart: "If you see 401s during bulk upsert on first run, try the canonical endpoint with trailing slash or update SDK once the patch lands." Marked as blocker for immediate onboarding flows.

Samira N.: I'll open an issue and attach the proxy traces + failing CI job. For now sample-app patched to call the canonical REST URL with trailing slash and explicit Authorization header as a temporary workaround.

Priya S.: I'll pick the SDK fix for JS (undici wrapper) and coordinate with Python/Go teams to ensure their HTTP clients don't drop auth on redirects. Also we'll add a small infra change request to redirect on server side to preserve auth (or not return a redirect for API calls).

Leo F.: Also note: we should include idempotency keys for bulk upserts in the long term so retries (accidental or from client) don't create duplicates. Add that as a follow-on.

Samira N.: Thanks everyone :raised_hands: — sample-app onboarding is unblocked with the temporary REST fix; tracking issue created and linked.
